title: Juniper and the Cipher
premise: Xanthe Vane, the concierge at the Saltmere Grand, has built a career on noticing what guests want to hide—until Elodie Marsh, a reclusive translator, vanishes from Room 407 and leaves behind a diary whose entries continue for three weeks after her disappearance. When Xanthe realizes the diary's later entries quote details from the police case file that were never made public, she understands the missing woman's confidant is the killer, feeding her a fabricated life to buy time before the tide exposes the body. Xanthe's investigation pulls in Detective Ivo Renner, who suspects her, and hotel owner Casimir Hale, whom she's loved for years and who is hiding a connection to Elodie. In the end, Xanthe stages a false diary entry to bait the killer into the hotel's sea caves, where the truth surfaces: Elodie staged her own disappearance to escape a blackmailer, but her accomplice—the concierge who trained Xanthe—murdered her to keep the hotel's buried secret, and dies trying to finish the story he started.
about_author: Mara Vane spent a decade working front desks in coastal hotels, collecting the small betrayals guests leave in lobby conversations. She writes mysteries about people who see everything and say nothing, from a house within earshot of the sea.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Signed Nothing
chapters.summary: Xanthe Vane's POV. A routine night at the Saltmere Grand: Xanthe smooths over a diplomat's indiscretion and quietly memorizes the habits of every guest, including reclusive translator Elodie Marsh in Room 407. When Elodie asks Xanthe to hold a sealed envelope 'until the tide turns,' the concierge's instinct for trouble stirs. Emotional beat: the comfort of competence shadowed by the first prickle of unease.

chapters.title: Room 407, Empty
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Elodie misses checkout; her room is immaculate, her luggage gone, her passport left behind—deliberately, Xanthe thinks. A housekeeper mentions a man in a grey coat on the fourth floor the night before. Xanthe reports the disappearance and, unable to help herself, pockets the room's forgotten reading glasses. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The Diary in the Safe
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Detective Ivo Renner arrives, sharp and suspicious of the too-observant concierge. Searching for Elodie's effects, they find a diary in the room safe—its final dated entry three days ago, long after she vanished. Renner seals it as evidence; Xanthe memorizes the last line. Emotional beat: the thrill of a real puzzle meeting professional dread.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Renner's POV. Renner works the shoreline and the guest register, finding Elodie checked out under a false name the morning she disappeared. His instinct says the hotel itself is complicit, and Xanthe's flawless memory makes her either his best witness or his best suspect. Emotional beat: wary attraction between two people who lie professionally.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The diary, leaked to her by a sympathetic clerk, describes Elodie's 'escape' in vivid detail—entries dated after her disappearance, quoting case-file details never made public. Someone is writing her life from the outside. Xanthe realizes the killer is close enough to read the investigation. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the case turns personal.

chapters.title: Casimir's Silence
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Hotel owner Casimir Hale—Xanthe's quiet, years-long almost-love—admits Elodie came to him months ago asking about the hotel's history and its 1974 fire. He refuses to say what he told her. Xanthe feels the first crack in her loyalty to the house that made her. Emotional beat: love measured against duty.

chapters.title: The Grey Coat
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe identifies the fourth-floor man: Wendell Pryce, a retired concierge who trained her years ago and left under a cloud. He's back in town, charming, asking about Elodie. Xanthe lies to him for the first time in her career—and hates how easily it comes. Emotional beat: the mentor's shadow over the student.

chapters.title: A Witness Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Renner's POV. Renner interviews staff and finds their accounts suspiciously aligned, as if rehearsed. He corners Xanthe with the diary's case-file quotations and accuses her of feeding the narrative. She counters with the grey coat. Uneasy, he agrees to share the file—off the record. Emotional beat: adversaries becoming reluctant allies.

chapters.title: The 1974 Fire
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the hotel archive, Xanthe reconstructs the fire that killed a chambermaid and was ruled accidental. Elodie's translation work included a memoir mentioning it. Someone in the hotel's past had everything to lose if the truth surfaced. Emotional beat: the past pressing up through the floorboards.

chapters.title: Entry Forty-One
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A new diary page appears in Xanthe's own mailbox—addressed to her, in Elodie's hand, warning: 'He writes me better than I wrote myself.' The killer knows Xanthe has the diary and is playing with her. Fear arrives, and she lets it sharpen her. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into strategy.

chapters.title: Two Truths in One Room
chapters.summary: Renner's POV. Renner discovers Elodie withdrew cash and bought a ferry ticket before vanishing—evidence she planned to leave, complicating the murder theory. But the diary entries continued after the ferry never sailed. He begins to suspect a staged disappearance gone wrong. Emotional beat: the case splitting into two incompatible stories.

chapters.title: The Confidant
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Reconstructing Elodie's last weeks, Xanthe finds the diary's early entries mention 'W.'—someone Elodie trusted with her fear of a blackmailer. Pryce fits, but so does Casimir, whose evasions have grown heavier. Xanthe confronts Casimir; he admits Elodie accused the hotel of covering up the fire's cause. Emotional beat: loyalty stretched to its breaking point.

chapters.title: What Xanthe Noticed First
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Reviewing her own nightly logs, Xanthe finds the detail she dismissed: Pryce's coat smelled of salt and cave air, though he claimed to have just arrived by train. He's been using the sea caves beneath the hotel—the ones the 1974 fire report sealed off. Emotional beat: the concierge's gift finally aimed like a weapon.

chapters.title: The Trap Is Baited
chapters.summary: Xanthe and Renner's alternating POV. They forge a diary entry 'found' in the caves, dated tomorrow, claiming Elodie hid the fire evidence there alive. Renner objects to the risk; Xanthe argues the killer can't resist closing the story he's been writing. They stake out the cave entrance. Emotional beat: two control freaks learning to trust.

chapters.title: Low Tide
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the caves, they find not Elodie but her hidden satchel: documents proving the fire was arson, set to hide a theft, with a young Pryce named in a suppressed statement. Then a light swings behind them—Pryce has followed the bait. Emotional beat: vindication and vertigo as the trap closes on both hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: The Story He Wrote
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, tense and claustrophobic. Pryce confesses with terrible calm: Elodie hired him to help her disappear from her blackmailer, but when she learned he was the arsonist, he drowned her in the cave pool and kept writing her diary to control the narrative—and to watch Xanthe, his best student, fail. Emotional beat: grief for Elodie, horror at the mentor.

chapters.title: The Turn of the Water
chapters.summary: Renner's POV. The tide floods the cave passage; Pryce tries to seal the exit and take the satchel. Renner is cut off; Xanthe, who knows the hotel's bones better than anyone, leads them through the old service tunnel from the fire's era. Pryce, refusing to let the story end without him, turns back into the rising water. Emotional beat: survival through the very knowledge that made her invisible.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Renner's POV. At dawn, the sea returns Elodie to the shore, and with her, closure. Pryce's body is found in the cave pool, the satchel's duplicate pages in his coat—he'd wanted the ending in his own hand. Renner closes the case and tells Xanthe she was never a suspect, only a mirror. Emotional beat: exhaustion, release, the strange grief of solved mysteries.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Reading Elodie's true final diary page—the one written before she vanished—Xanthe finds not fear but hope: plans for a small flat in Lisbon, a life after hiding. She mails the diary to Elodie's sister with a letter telling the whole truth. Emotional beat: mourning someone she only knew on paper.

chapters.title: Casimir, Unlocked
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Casimir, unburdened by the fire's secret, finally tells Xanthe why he kept silent: shame for his father's arson, and fear of losing her respect. Xanthe admits she stayed invisible her whole life for the same reason. They choose each other, cautiously, without the hotel standing between them. Emotional beat: love that no longer requires secrecy.

chapters.title: The Concierge's Rule
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe revises her one rule: never take a case you can't close becomes never take a case that closes you. She trains a new hire to notice everything and say more than she ever did, and returns Elodie's reading glasses to Room 407, now let to a guest who signs her name proudly. Emotional beat: quiet transformation.

chapters.title: Until the Tide Turns
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, epilogue. Months later, a sealed envelope arrives at the desk addressed in Elodie's hand—sent before her death, held by a ferry office. Inside: a thank-you, and one last entry predicting that Xanthe would be the one to finish her story. Xanthe smiles, pockets nothing, and rings the front desk bell. Emotional beat: peace, and the promise of the next story.
